_comment: How the grading layer treats each table when looking for collateral damage.
Damage is a row the agent inserted, deleted or modified that the gold path
left untouched. Rows the gold path also touched are the agent's work area: each
may end as it started, which expected_final_state.json then judges, or as the
gold path left it, so an agent that reaches the right outcome by a different
route is not penalised for the route it took. A third value in one is damage.

_ignore_reason: Reads must be free: an agent may look at anything as often as it likes, so
nothing a read advances can count as damage. id_allocator moves when an
extra create is issued, but the row that create produced is caught on its
own account. scenario is the immutable clock.
_append_reason: claims is append-only in the real system and a resubmission genuinely
leaves a second row. The outcome is asserted through the latest_claims
view, so an extra claim row is a different route to the same place. A
modification to an existing claim row is still damage, and so is any new
row in a table not listed here - initiating a transfer nobody asked for
has consequences, so transfer_requests is deliberately absent.
